about: Transparent L-band interpretation rules. Thresholds describe typical NISAR L-band behaviour; they are not an official land-cover classification. Classes are tested top to bottom; the first match wins.

classes.label: Water or very smooth ground
classes.plain: Calm water or very smooth ground: the radar wave bounces away like off a mirror, so almost nothing comes back.

classes.label: Buildings or rocks
classes.plain: Buildings or rocks: walls and ground act like corner reflectors and send the wave straight back.

classes.label: Dense vegetation
classes.plain: Dense vegetation: leaves and branches scatter the wave in all directions, giving a strong HV signal.

classes.label: Shrubs or sparse trees
classes.plain: Shrubs or sparse trees: some scattering inside the vegetation, weaker than a forest.

classes.label: Open ground or fields
classes.plain: Open ground or fields: the wave mostly reflects off the surface; there is little vegetation volume.

change.label: Vegetation loss
change.plain: Since {prev} the vegetation signal fell by {abs} dB — consistent with burned or removed vegetation.

change.label: Vegetation gain
change.plain: Since {prev} the vegetation signal rose by {abs} dB — growing plants or wetter ground.

global.label: Approximate · ~500 m, estimated from NASA GIBS imagery

gibs_model.about: dB = a + b*ln(1+G) + c*ln(1+R) on GIBS 'NISAR_L2_Geocoded_Polarimetric_Covariance' tiles (zoom <= 8). Fitted on Spain 2026-07-26; checked on Spain 2026-10-18 (HV ±0.8 dB) and Muğla (HV ±1.0 dB).
